title: Dental PPO Plans Missing-Tooth Clause Credit for Requested Estimates
content:
For a pre-treatment estimate requested anew under the Dental PPO Plans (a requested estimate), the months credited toward the missing-tooth clause follow where the replaced tooth was lost:
- when the service records of the person's earlier DHMO enrollment show an extraction of that tooth on the recorded extraction date, the clause credit is the calendar months from the month that DHMO coverage took effect through the month it ended, both months counted;
- when they show no such extraction and the enrollment shows documented prior coverage months whose prior coverage end date is on or after the extraction date and no more than 63 calendar days before the coverage effective date, the clause credit is those documented months;
- otherwise no months are credited.

The months credited are added to the months of continuous enrollment, and so decide the estimated patient cost on such an estimate.

The person's earlier DHMO enrollment is the person's own terminated enrollment in Cascade's Prepaid Dental HMO Plans, matched by name and date of birth, that ended on the day before the Dental PPO enrollment's coverage effective date (a move from the DHMO with no break in coverage). The person's DHMO services are read only from that enrollment's own service records, never from another enrollment of the same subscriber.

### Judgement points
- The DHMO record must show the same tooth and the same date as the extraction date recorded for the replaced tooth; an extraction of another tooth, or on another date, does not give the DHMO credit.
- The documented-months credit needs both dates: an end date on or after the extraction date, and no more than 63 calendar days (the figure on every Dental PPO plan) before the coverage effective date.

### Example (hypothetical, clause of 24 months)
DHMO enrollment from 1 January to 30 September with the extraction of the tooth recorded on its service records; Dental PPO effective 1 October; issue date 1 March of the following year: 9 months credited plus 5 months of continuous enrollment gives 14, short of 24.
